assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's Sr-lattice realisation, reach roughly 1e-18 fractional uncertainty. This is a clear, original, lasting advance in atomic precision measurement, with consequences for time keeping, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early Sr clocks; Ye drove the record accuracy and the many-body clock work. A two-person share is natural. Other contributors such as Hall and Hansch were recognised in 2005 for combs, and the supplied credit does not list further names.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories worldwide have confirmed the performance. Comparisons between clocks are routine and a redefinition of the SI second is under discussion, so the timing is right.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to wait for the formal redefinition of the second.
Possible competing claims from ion-clock groups, which are outside this candidate's credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics brought strong light-matter coupling to superconducting circuits and is the working architecture of most superconducting quantum processors. It is a conceptually clean transfer of cavity-QED ideas into a solid-state setting, with major downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the key theory with Girvin and Huang, Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. Girvin, Devoret and others played large roles and are not in the credited list, so the fair allocation is somewhat open. The chosen three correspond to the theory proposal plus the experimental demonstrations.
assessment.maturity: The architecture has been reproduced by many groups and is the basis of large commercial and academic devices. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits adds context but covers a different discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap of credit with Girvin, Devoret and Nakamura outside the credited names.
Possible concern that recognition so soon after the 2025 circuit prize may look repetitive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a field of topological band theory with symmetry protection, with experiments in HgTe wells and the later 3D materials. It is highly original and broadly influential across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal, Molenkamp's group with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang realised it in HgTe. Hasan (and also Moore, Balents, Roy, Fu and Hsieh) are central for the 3D case, so any prize needs a cut that omits real contributors. I select the theory plus the first experimental realisation.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many materials and platforms over almost two decades, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is mature, though the topological field was recently honoured in 2016.
uncertainties: Substantial unresolved allocation between the 2D and 3D parts, and between Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang.
The 2016 prize may reduce appetite for another topological prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle flat bands and the observed correlated insulator and superconducting states opened twistronics and a widely studied tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. The idea is original and the physical picture is compact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero's group observed the correlated and superconducting phases in 2018. This three-person split is clean. Cao and others in the experimental team and other theorists are not credited, and I cannot judge their share here.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups with rich follow-up, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet settled. Timing is fairly early.
uncertainties: Unresolved pairing mechanism of the superconductivity.
Prize may be premature compared with more settled topics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation made controllable entangled many-body quantum systems practical. It stands as a foundation of quantum information processing in atomic physics, which I can assess from the atomic-physics side.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal; Blatt's group realised gates, teleportation and scalable control. Wineland and Monroe are major contributors to the ion-trap programme and are outside the credited names, which makes the allocation delicate. B019 is a related candidate with the same names; I treat this one as the ion-specific entry.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several independent ion-trap groups and commercial machines. Quantum information was recognised in 2012 and 2022, so a further award needs a clear argument that this is distinct.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with candidate B019 on atomic quantum information.
Role of Wineland and Monroe outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical-lattice quantum simulation realised Hubbard-type models with ultracold atoms, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and single-site quantum gas microscopes. It is an original way to study many-body physics with controlled parameters.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and collaborators proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott transition experiment and developed the microscope. Cirac is also a candidate for the theory side but I limit the share to three. Jaksch is a key theorist outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Many groups reproduce and extend the work and it is increasingly used for questions not tractable classically, but the strongest application results are still emerging. Recognition is timely, with BEC already honoured in 2001.
uncertainties: Credit for the Mott insulator proposal, which involved Jaksch and others not listed.
Whether the field has delivered a single decisive discovery rather than a toolbox.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: X-ray free-electron lasers deliver femtosecond, highly coherent hard X-ray pulses, enabling time-resolved structure, atomic and molecular dynamics and nonlinear X-ray physics. It is a major instrument advance with broad science impact, partly overlapping with ultrafast methods I know.
assessment.attribution: SASE theory and design involved Bonifacio, Pellegrini, Narducci, Kondratenko and Saldin, Kim, and the TESLA test facility under Rossbach, with the LCLS realisation. The credited names omit some foundational contributors, which makes a clean prize configuration doubtful. I choose those with the strongest link in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: LCLS, SACLA and European XFEL operate routinely with abundant scientific output. The technology is mature, though the case is mostly about an instrument rather than a discovery.
uncertainties: Whether an accelerator and instrument achievement fits the prize criteria.
Large unresolved credit among accelerator physicists, not all in the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Strongly interacting Fermi gases and the BEC-BCS crossover created a tunable quantum fluid that models unitary matter relevant to neutron stars and superconductors. The control of interactions through Feshbach resonances is a significant and lasting contribution.
assessment.attribution: Grimm, Ketterle and Salomon, with the late Deborah Jin who is not in the credited list, produced molecular BECs and the crossover. Jin's central role makes a fair configuration difficult since she cannot be awarded posthumously.
assessment.maturity: The results are confirmed in several laboratories and compare well with theory, including the universal thermodynamics. Timing is mature, but the loss of a central contributor weakens the case.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Deborah Jin from any laureate list.
Overlap with ultracold-atom physics recognised in 2001.
